name: Ex falso quodlibet (¬P ⊢ P→Q)
description: From a denied antecedent, anything follows: ¬P ⊢ (P→Q). The proof is a single insertion — ~[ (P) ] (which is ¬P, and also the empty scroll's antecedent) admits ~[ (Q) ] into its negative interior by the insertion rule, producing the scroll ~[ (P) ~[(Q)] ] = P→Q. A clean illustration of the one place insertion is licensed: inside a negative context, where you may entertain anything without yet asserting it.
